name: discomfort
quote: Public speaking is outside my comfort zone.
description: Being outside the tolerable zone of physical, social, or mental expectations.
perceptions: The current situation is considered unpleasant in some way.

comparisons.description: Discomfort is a negative perception about the situation, but it doesn't always cause anxiety or fear. For instance, you could be uncomfortable about a social situation, but if you can just walk away and not deal with those people again, you may not have anxiety. On the other hand, discomfort with people you know could cause anxiety from not being sure how to deal with the situation.

Pain is something you'll do a lot to avoid again in the future. Discomfort is an annoyance that may be the price of admission for something you enjoy. For example, some people find a 6-hour drive so mentally painful they would rather fly, while others find it a minor discomfort that doesn't stop them.

'Dissatisfaction' is a limited sensation that something specific did not meet your expectations, while 'discomfort' is a generalized sense that there's something that needs to be improved right now. For instance, you could be dissatisfied about the job you gluing the handle back on the mug, but just decide to let your spouse re-do it later and not feel uncomfortable about the overall situation.

'Discomfort' is the sensation that drives an impulse to want to improve it. For example, perhaps you're so dissatisfied about something that you decide it takes you outside your zone what's tolerable. You're now in a perceived state of discomfort, which generally means that a desire will arise to exit that state somehow.

variations.name: mental discomfort
variations.description: A perception that your mental state is outside of a tolerable zone such that you have a moderately negative outlook on the situation.
perceptions: I'm anxious, bored, tired, having a bad day, etc.

guidance.description: We all have a threshold for being uncomfortable. How high that threshold is varies from person to person. The higher your threshold, the more comfortable you are with being uncomfortable. However, there are steps you can take to make stepping outside your comfort zone easier, regardless of your natural comfort level.

examples: hearing a piece of news that bothers you

variations.name: social discomfort
variations.description: A perception that the immediate social situation is outside of your tolerable zone or that it could become that way at any moment.
perceptions: Something's happening socially that I view as moderately negative.
This is the kind of situation where something moderately negative could happen.

guidance.description: Although awkward conversations may seem difficult, they can be good opportunities to practice making small talk and handling conflict.

examples: at a party where you feel out of place
seeing a couple argue in public
someone makes a comment you consider inappropriate

variations.name: physical discomfort
variations.description: The recognition that your body is experiencing something outside of your preferred tolerance zone or a very minor pain.
perceptions: Part of my body is sensing something outside of my comfort zone.

guidance.description: If there's no obvious reason for an extended period of physical discomfort, you might consider when to see a doctor.

examples: sitting on a hard surface for a long time
the temperature is a little too high or low

commentaries.quote: Everyone has different levels of tolerance for different kinds of discomfort before crossing into their 'discomfort' state. When you reach that place, the instinct is to adjust something to make it less uncomfortable.
Temporary discomfort is an investment in your future self

My comfort zone is like a little bubble around me, and I've pushed it in different directions and made it bigger and bigger until these objectives that seemed totally crazy eventually fall within the realm of the possible.
Uncomfortable doesn't mean bad, uncomfortable simply means you're doing something you haven't done before.
